Hannah (Eng): Hi team — urgent payroll question. I was seconded to Dublin for 10 weeks (2026-11-01 -> 2026-01-09) and my November payroll shows US Social Security withholding as usual. My manager said we should have split contributions with Irish PRSI while I was onsite. Can this be corrected?
Lina (People Ops): Thanks for flagging. Did you have a formal secondment agreement and did People Ops update your work location in Ripley before the Nov payroll cutoff?
Hannah (Eng): Secondment addendum signed 2026-10-28 and Ripley location updated 2026-10-29 13:12 ET. I also uploaded passport + Irish PPSN on 10/30. I assumed payroll would switch to Irish payroll for the secondment period.
Priya (Payroll): Quick checks: 1) Did the days in Ireland exceed 183? (doesn't sound like it) 2) Was there an active Eire payroll enrollment for you before pr-20261101 cutoff? If not, our system may have defaulted to US run. We can request a correction but need Eire payroll confirmation and advice from tax.
Eoin (Eire Payroll): We show no active employee record for Hannah at the 2026-11-01 payrun snapshot. Enrollment request arrived 2026-10-31 17:45 UTC and activated 2026-11-10. Activation after the run explains default US withholding. We can process a retroactive correction but need confirmation of employment tax residency and social security coverage rules (S1/A1 or bilateral agreement).
Alicia (Tax Counsel): High-level: social security for short-term secondments depends on treaty and EU rules. For employees temporarily posted to Ireland, A1 certificate or S1 may exempt local PRSI and keep US coverage for the period, or vice versa. If Irish PRSI should have applied, we can file amended Irish payroll returns and reverse US FICA withholding via corrected payroll. We'll loop in our international payroll advisor to confirm social security positioning and whether reimbursements are needed.

Priya (Payroll): Action plan: 1) Payroll to submit a retrospective reallocation request to Eire payroll and external advisor (submitted). 2) Tax to confirm whether A1 certificate or bilateral rule applies. 3) If Irish payroll should have applied, process reversal of US FICA and reissue under Eire payroll (with PRSI). 4) If US coverage was correct, provide confirmation and close.
Hannah (Eng): Thanks. Concerned about end-of-year reports — will W-2 be amended if FICA is reversed? I need clean docs for mortgage and OSS forms.
Alicia (Tax Counsel): If we reverse FICA we will issue corrected W-2 (W-2c) and file amended US payroll returns (941-X) accordingly. On the Irish side we will file corrected PAYE/PRSI returns. Timeline depends on advisor but expect 10-20 business days after approval.
Eoin (Eire Payroll): Submitted case EP-2027-88 to external Irish advisor. Please DM PPSN and upload the secondment addendum to ticket PO-2027-234.
Lina (People Ops): Created PO-2027-234 and invited Payroll + Tax + Eire payroll. Hannah please DM sensitive docs.
